subject: APAC remittance corridor — fee allocation & FX anchor date
messages:
From: APAC Payments <payments@acme-apac.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Tan <sofia.tan@acme-apac.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Remittance path question for Redwood invoice (Nov)

Hi Vivek,

We received the invoice for November and are preparing the wire. A couple of quick questions before we initiate:

1) Our bank tells us there may be an intermediary / correspondent bank in the routing. Can you confirm which correspondent bank will be used for USD wires into Redwood’s Singapore collection account?

2) How should we set the fee allocation? Our treasury prefers SHA by default, but they warned that intermediate fees could be deducted by the correspondent leaving Redwood with less than the invoice amount.

3) For FX: we will originate in SGD and our bank will convert to USD. What is Redwood’s policy for the FX anchor/date for crediting the invoice (invoice paid date)? Is it the value date posted by your bank or the originating bank’s conversion date?

We want to avoid short pays and delays — appreciate any concrete instructions. I attached the draft remittance we planned to send.

Thanks,

Liam (on behalf of APAC Payments team)
[Attachment: sample-remittance.txt (text)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: APAC Payments <payments@acme-apac.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 06:42:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Remittance path question for Redwood invoice (Nov)

Hi Liam / Sofia —

Thanks for the heads-up. Short answers up front, full details below:

- Primary correspondent (likely): Citibank N.A., Singapore (Swift: CITISGSG).
- Fee allocation options: OUR (customer covers all fees) is safest to ensure full invoice amount lands with us; SHA can result in intermediary deductions.
- FX anchor/date: we credit the invoice based on the value date funds are made available into our SGD receiving account post-conversion — in practice that is the date the USD hits our account after the correspondent/nostro processing.

Marissa, Rachel — looping you in to provide final collection details and confirm the recommended fee code for Acme APAC.

Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
[redwood.ai]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: APAC Payments <payments@acme-apac.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 08:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Remittance path question for Redwood invoice (Nov)

Hi Liam / Sofia —

Thanks for flagging this. Confirming collection instructions and practical guidance below. Please follow these exactly to avoid short pays.

1) Collection account (SGP) — use these coordinates if you are sending USD after your bank converts from SGD: 

  Bank name: Standard Chartered Bank, Singapore Branch
  Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Inc.
  Beneficiary account (USD nostro): 006-123456-78
  SWIFT: SCBLSGSG
  Correspondent bank (nostro intermediary): Citibank N.A., Singapore (CITISGSG) — note: some banks route via Citi as the intermediary.

2) Fee allocations — choose one option and indicate clearly on the instruction: 
  - OUR: Acme pays all charges (sender + correspondents + receiving). This ensures Redwood receives the full invoice amount. Recommended when you want to guarantee gross payment.
  - SHA: Charges are shared — sending bank charges you; correspondent/receiving bank charges deducted from the credited amount. This is the default for many corporates but risks short pays when intermediaries take fees.
  - BEN: All charges deducted from the beneficiary (not recommended).

3) If you must use SHA (internal policy), please add an overpay buffer of ~USD 20 to cover potential intermediary deductions OR explicitly ask your sending bank to route via Citibank Singapore and to request copies of the MT103 with fee details so we can reconcile.

4) FX anchor / crediting date — operational detail: if you originate in SGD and the originating bank converts to USD before sending, Redwood will mark the invoice as paid on the date the USD funds post to our receiving account in Singapore (i.e., the correspondent/nostro value date). Please include your bank’s conversion reference on the remittance so we can match.

5) VAT / tax notes — we are not registered for GST/VAT in Singapore for this contract. We will issue a tax-exclusive invoice. If local VAT/GST applies, Acme should self-assess per local rules. We can add a line-item to the invoice that says “Customer to self-assess local VAT/GST where applicable” and include your local VAT id on the PDF if you send it to us.

Attachments: I’ve attached the updated collection grid (redwood_collection_grid_SGP.xlsx) and a sample remittance text that formats the MT103 references we need.

Action items for Acme:
- Prefer OUR to guarantee full credit; otherwise include the MT103 reference and consider USD20 buffer.
- Send back the final remittance text before you transmit so we can pre-match.

If you want, we can accept payment to our USD account in the US instead (no intermediary in APAC), but that will trigger additional FX routing on your bank side and potentially higher fees — let us know if you want that alternative and I’ll pass US account details.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance — Collections, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_collection_grid_SGP.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: APAC Payments <payments@acme-apac.com>

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — we’ll do OUR for this wire to avoid deductions. A couple follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm the exact narrative text to put in the remittance (we normally have a single free-text field called "reference") — should it include the invoice number and buyer code?
2) We will convert SGD -> USD at our bank; can you confirm whether Redwood needs the originating bank’s conversion reference (eg TRN12345) vs. the MT103 trace number?

We will send the wire tomorrow morning (SGT) and upload the remittance advice. Attached is our final remittance draft for your quick review.

Liam
APAC Payments, Acme APAC

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Remittance path question for Redwood invoice (Nov)

Hi Liam / Sofia —

Perfect — thanks for choosing OUR. For the remittance reference please use the following template in the single free-text reference field: 

  "INV 202611-ACME-<your PO or buyer code> | ACME APAC Pte Ltd"

Please also paste at least one of the following in the payment details or notes field (we can accept either):
  - originating bank conversion reference (e.g., TRN12345) OR
  - MT103 Trace / end-to-end (e2e) field (if your bank provides MT103).

Either one is sufficient for our reconciliation team; MT103 is preferred when available because it contains fee splits.

Once the wire is sent, please upload the payment advice to the Drive link below or attach to the HubSpot deal and we’ll mark the invoice as paid on the value date the USD posts to our account.

Drive upload: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/invoices/ACME/2026/ACME_invoice_202611.pdf
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-EXP-2026-Q4

We’ll confirm on receipt and share the credited amount and MT103 lines if anything looks off.

Thanks again —
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance — Collections, Redwood Inference
